rows.author: E047
rows.title_short: Mass Lay-off
rows.abstract: DESCRIBED THE WORSENING SITUATION OF THE FILIPINO WORKERS WHICH WAS AGGRAVATED BY THE CURRENT GLOBAL FINANCIAL CRISIS.  HE NOTED THAT THE GOVERNMENT'S \"ECONOMIC RESILIENCY PLAN\" AND THE DOLE'S \"CONTINGENCY MEASURES\" WERE ONLY MEANT TO BENEFIT THE CAPITALIST BUSINESSMEN TO THE DETRIMENT OF THE INTEREST OF THE POOR WORKERS.  ENUMERATED LONG-TERM ACTION THAT THE GOVERNMENT MUST DO:  1. PROTECT LOCAL EMPLOYMENT; 2.  CREATE LOCAL JOB OPPORTUNITIES BY SUPPORTING THE SMALL & MEDIUM ENTERPRISES AND PROMOTING AGRICULTURE; 3.  LOWER THE PRICES OF BASIC GOODS AND SERVICES BY ABOLISHING EVAT & OIL DEREGULATION; 4. MORATORIUM ON THE WORKERS' PAYMENT OF WITHHOLDING TAX AND TAX REFUNDS; 5.  INCREASE THE BUDGET FOR SOCIAL SERVICES; 6.  SECURE THE INSURANCE FUNDS MEANT FOR FILIPINO WORKERS; AND 7. IMPLEMENT A GENUINE AGRARIAN REFORM PROGRAM THAT WILL STRENGTHEN AGRICULTURAL SECTOR THEREBY CREATING JOBS AND INDUSTRIES.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2009-02-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Maza and Manifestation by Rep. Escudero.  Referred to the appropriated committee.

rows.author: D099
rows.title_short: Kidnap - For - Ranson As National Security Issue
rows.abstract: UNDERSCORED THE CONTINUING OCCURRENCE AND THREAT OF KIDNAPPING IN SULU, BASILAN, TAWI-TAWI AND ZAMBOANGA AND CITED THE NAMES OF THE VICTIMS AND PROMINENT PERSONALITIES THAT HAVE BEEN ABDUCTED.  STATED THAT KIDNAPPING IN THESE AREAS IS A GRUESOME REALITY THAT THE GOVERNMENT NEEDS TO IMMEDIATELY ADDRESS BECAUSE OF ITS TRAUMATIC EFFECT ON THE VICITIMS AND THEIR FAMILIES AND THE SCOURGE THAT IT POSES.  INQUIRED ON THE ACTION TAKEN BY THE PNP AND THE LOCAL AUTHORITIES, LIKE IN THE CASE OF PO1 OSAMA ISMAEL.  URGED THE MEMBERS TO CONDUCT AN INVESTIGATION INTO THE LATEST SPATE OF KIDNAPPINGS.  INQUIRED ON THE NEED TO REVIEW THE POLICIES OF GOVERNMENT PERTAINING TO KIDNAPPING FOR RANSOM, TO INCLUDE INQUIRING INTO THE MANDATE, CAPACITY AND PERFORMANCE OF THE POLICE ANTI-CRIME EMERGENCY RESPONSE (PACER) AND TO ASSESS THE POLICIES, CAPABILITIES AND RESPONSE OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND THE PNP.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on MINDANAO AFFAIRS since 2009-02-09
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Cerilles.  Referred to the Committees on Mindanao Affairs, Peace, Reconciliation and Unity; Public Order and Safety; Local Government and National Defense and Security.

rows.author: A027
rows.title_full: SPEECH OF US SENATOR INUYE, SUPPORTING FILIPINO VETERANS OF WORLD WAR II
rows.title_short: Philippine Veterans Of World War I I
rows.abstract: READ TO THE BODY THE SPEECH OF SENATOR DANIEL K. INOUYE OF HAWAII RE:  THE STATUS OF THE VETERANS EQUITY BILL IN THE US SENATE WHICH SINGLED OUT THE FILIPINO WAR VETERANS.  ADDED THAT THE STIMULUS PACKAGE DOES NOT CONTAIN A COMPENSATON PACKAGE FOR FILIPINOS BUT IS MERELY AN ACT OF RECOGNITION.  HOWEVER, HE SAID THAT IT WAS PROMISED THAT COMPENSATION SHALL COME LATER.  REPLIED THAT S180 MILLION WAS INITIALLY APPROPRIATED FOR FILIPINO VETERANS.  SHARED HIS HOPE THAT THE FILIPINO SOLDIERS WHO WERE INCARCERATED IN BATAAN WILL BE GIVEN JUST COMPENSATION AND BACK PAY BY THE US GOVERNMENT.  CLARIFIED THAT THE FUND FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE STIMULUS BILL IS NOT SUFFICIENT BUT THAT IN RECOGNITION OF THE VALOR OF FILIPINOS IN BATAAN, SENATOR INOUYE PROMISED TO SECURE MONEY FOR THE PURPOSE.  EXPRESED HOPE THAT WITH THE ENLARGED DEMOCRATIC MEMBERSHIP IN THE HOUSE, THE BILL WILL BE IMMEDIATELY APPROVED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on VETERANS AFFAIRS AND WELFARE since 2009-02-17
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Golez.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.title_full: WORLD BANK REPORT ON CORRUPTION IN WB-FUNDED PUBLIC WORKS PROJECTS
rows.title_short: Alleged Bribery In The World Bank Funded Projects
rows.abstract: COMMENDED THE HOUSE COMMITTEE ON PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS FOR NOT ENTERTAINING AN ALLEGATION THAT FIRST GENTLEMAN MIKE ARROYO WAS INVOLVED IN GRAFT-RIDDLED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS INASMUCH AS RELIABLE DOCUMENTS OR WITNESSES WERE LACKING.  STRESSED THAT CONGRESS SHOULD NOT CONSIDER MATTERS WHICH CANNOT HELP IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE COUNTRY.  TOGETHER WITH REP. KHO, INITIALLY DISCUSSED THE PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE AND BIDDING PROCESSES OF THE DPWH VIS-A-VIS THAT OF THE WORLD BANK.  STRESSED THAT THE MONEY BORROWED WOULD BE PAID BACK WITH INTEREST AND THAT THE WORLD BANK HAS NO RIGHT TO IMPOSE UPON THE DPWH WHAT TO DO WITH THE MONEY AND THE CHOICE OF CONTRACTOR.  ADDED THAT THE BIDDING PROCESS OF THE DPWH IS ABOVE BOARD AND THAT THE BRIBEY ISSUE OF THE WORLD BANK IS ALL ACCUSATION AND WITHOUT EVIDENCE.  OPINED THAT THE WORLD BANK WOULD LIKE TO CREATE AN ISSUE OUT OF NOTHING AND THAT IT WOULD BE PREMATURE FOR CONGRESS TO INVESTIGATE THE MATTER.  SAID THAT THE DPWH DID NOT SUSPEND ANY CONTRACTOR BECAUSE IT HAS NO BASIS FOR DOING SUCH.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BANKS AND FINANCIAL INTERMEDIARIES since 2009-02-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Kho, Fua and Cagas.  Referred to the Committees on Good Government, and Banks and Financial Intermediaries

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: EFFECTS OF GLOBAL FINANCIAL CRISIS ON MIGRANT WORKERS
rows.title_short: Loans For Retrenched O F Ws
rows.abstract: FOCUSED ON THE GOVERNMENT'S LABOR EXPORT POLICY AND THE ADVERSE EFFECTS OF THE PREVAILING WORLD ECONOMIC CRISIS TO OFWs.  CITED DATA FROM THE OWWA - OFWs RETRENCHED FROM DIFFERENT COUNTRIES WHICH IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE TEN-FOLD AS BUSINESS ABROAD SUFFER RECESSION.  CLAIMED THAT THE ARROYO ADMINISTRATION REFUSES TO PROVIDE A GENUINE AND LONG-TERM CONTINGENCY PROGRAM FOR THE DISPLACED OFWs, INSTEAD, CITED ADMIN.ORDER 248, \"RECIPROCITY PROGRAM\" FOR A FILIPINO EXPATRIATE LIVELIHOOD SUPPORT FUND.  INQUIRED ON THE GOVERNMENT'S INTENTION TO DANGLE FUND FROM THE OFWs MANDATORY CONTRIBUTION.  STATED THAT THE LOSS OF OFWs BASIC HUMAN RIGHTS, CAN BE ATTRIBUTED TO THE GOVERNMENT'S ADHERENCE TO A LABOR EXPORT POLICY WHICH CONTRAVENES THE BASIC PROVISIONS OF THE CONSTITUTION AND IS A DESPERATE ATTEMPT TO ADOPT A GLOBALIZED ECONOMY THAT PERPETRATES \"CHEAP LABOR\".  CONTENDED THAT REMITTANCES ONLY ARTIFICIALLY PROPS UP THE ECONOMY AND THE \"STRENGTHENING\" OF THE PESO PRESENTS DIFFICULTIES TO FILIPINO EXPORTERS PARTICULARLY THOSE USING LOCAL INPUTS, AND DOMESTIC PRODUCERS COMPETING WITH IMPORTED GOODS.  EXPLAINED THAT OFWs CONTRIBUTION TO FOREIGN EXCHANGE RESOURCES WAS NOT BENEFICIAL AFTER ALL BECAUSE THESE ARE USED MOSTLY FOR FOREIGN DEBT SERVICING PAYMENT OF IMPORTS OF FOREIGN-DOMINATED INDUSTRIES AND OTHER UNPRODUCTIVE ENDS.  ARGUED THAT LABOR MIGRATION AND DEPENDENCE TO REMITTANCES ARE NOT VIABLE LONG-TERM SOLUTIONS TO THE COUNTRY'S CURRENT ECONOMIC AND FINANCIAL PROBLEMS.  DEMANDED AN END TO THIS KIND OF POLICY AND SUGGESTED RECOMMENDATIONS NAMELY:  LEGAL AND FINACIAL ASSISTANCE TO DISPLACED OFWs'; CREATING LOCAL JOBS, INCREASING THE BUDGET FOR SOCIAL SERVICES; AND INITIATING GENUINE AGARARIAN REFORM AND OPENING UP INDUSTRIES.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2009-02-24
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Cerilles, Alfelor, Climaco, Cruz-Gonzales and Rodriguez.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F075
rows.title_short: Illegal Gambling Operations In Camarines Norte
rows.abstract: REFERRED TO THE ILLEGAL ONLINE GAMBLING OPERATIONS CONDUCTED IN HER DISTRICT BY MERIDIEN VISTA GAMING CORP.  UNDERSCORED THAT THE CERTIFICATE OF REGISTRATION IS ONLY TO ENGAGE IN GAMING OPERATIONS AS A CAGAYAN SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE AND FREEPORT ENTERPRISE TO BE LOCATED WITHIN THE ZONE AREA OF STA. ANA, CAGAYAN.  POINTED OUT THAT NOTHING IN RA7922 GRANTS CEZA ANY POWER TO EXERCISE BEYOND THE CAGAYAN SPECIAL ECONOMIC ZONE SO THAT THERE IS NO LEGAL JUSTIFICATION FOR ITS ACT OF OVEREXTENDING ITS LICENSING POWERS TO AREAS NOT WITHN ITS JURISDICTION.  SAID THAT MERIDIEN ALSO INVOKED THE TAX INCENTIVE GRANTED BY LAW TO ESCAPE LOCAL TAXES.  SAID THAT BUSINESSES MUST SECURE LOCAL LEGISLATIVE RESOLUTION OR PERMIS/LICENSES BEFORE OPERATING AND CONGRESS SHOULD NOT ABDICATE ITS SOLE POWER TO DECLARE WHICH GAMBLING ACTIVITIES ARE LEGAL AND WHERE THEY CAN BE OPERATED.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2009-02-18
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Magsaysay and Alfelor; Manifestation by Rep. Padilla.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: DISAPPEARANCE OF MR. LEO VELASCO
rows.title_short: Human Rights Violations On Peace Consultants And Advocates And Activists
rows.abstract: SPOKE ABOUT THE EXTRAJUDICIAL MEASURES BEING EMPLOYED BY THE ARROYO ADMINISTRATION, SPECIFICALLY THE DISAPPEARANCE OF LEO VELASCO.  ARGUED THAT HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS HAVE PROLIFERATED BECAUSE THE GOVERNMENT HAS ABANDONED PEACE TALKS BY FORMALLY SUSPENDING THE GRP-NDF PEACE NEGOTIATIONS IN 2004 AND SHIFTED TO THE DEMOBILIZATION, DISARMAMENT AND REHABILITATION POLICY IN 2008 WHICH CONSIDERS WAR AS THE PRIMARY SOLUTION TO AN ARMED CONFLICT.  CONSIDERING THAT ENFORCED DISAPPEARANCE IS ONE OF THE WORST FORMS OF HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS, REP. CASINO URGED CONGRESS TO IMMEDIATELY PASS THE BILL TO CRIMINALIZE SUCH VIOLATION.  APPEALED TO RESUME THE PEACE PROCESS AND NOT TO RESORT TO EXTRAJUDICIAL MEASURES AGAINST THE PERCEIVED ENEMIES.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2009-02-24

rows.author: F020
rows.title_full: ALLEGED CORRUPTION COMMITTED BY EASTERN SAMAR GOV. BEN EVARDONE
rows.title_short: Gov. Evardone's Abuse Of Power And Blatant Corruption
rows.abstract: TALKED ON THE BLATANT CORRUPTIONS THROUGH DECEITFUL SCHEMES AND ABUSE OF POWER ILLICITLY PRACTICED AND PERPETRATED BY EASTERN SAMAR GOV. BEN EVARDONE ON THE ISSUES OF THE P173 MILLION LOAN FOR THE PURCHASE OF HEAVY EQUIPMENT, THE P100 MILLION CALAMITY FUND AND THE ISSUANCE OF SMALL SCALE MINING PERMIT. REQUESTED TO CONDUCT A CONGRESSIONAL INQUIRY ON THE MATTER.

rows.author: E003
rows.title_short: Issues On The Visiting Forces Agreement
rows.abstract: TALKED ON HOW THE US GOVERNMENT HAD BLATANTLY DISREGARDED AND DISRESPECTED THE PHILIPPINES' SOVEREIGNTY WHEN THE FORMER REFUSES TO TURN OVER THE CUSTODY OF CONVICTED RAPIST CORPORAL DANIEL SMITH ASIDE FROM THE FACT THAT EVEN PRES. MACAPAGAL-ARROYO WAS NOT ACKNOWLEDGED BY US PRES. BARACK OBAMA DURING THE ANNUAL PRAYER BREAKFAST IN WASHINGTON, D.C. DANIEL SMITH WHO HAS BEEN PLACED UNDER THE CUSTODY OF THE PHILIPPINE AUTHORITIES.

rows.author: A027
rows.title_short: Philippine Merchant Marine Academy
rows.abstract: TOOK THE FLOOR TO COMMEND THE PHILIPPINE MERCHANT MARINE ACADEMY (PMMA) FOR ITS ACHIEVEMENT IN THE FIELD OF MARITIME EDUCATION AND PUSHED FOR THE PASSAGE OF SOUND LAWS THAT WILL IMPROVE THE NATION'S MARITIME AND SHIPPING INDUSTRY.

rows.author: D085
rows.title_short: Custody Of Lance Corporal Daniel Smith
rows.abstract: STATED THAT THE PURPOSE OF HER SPEECH IS TO RAISE THE VOICES OF WOMEN ON THE ISSUE OF CUSTODY AND DETENTION OF U.S. SERVICEMAN LANCE CORPORAL DANIEL SMITH WHO WAS FOUND GUILTY OF THE CRIME OF RAPE AGAINST A FILIPINA IN SUBIC, OLONGAPO, AND HOW THE VISITING FORCES AGREEMENT (VFA) REMAINS TO BE A HINDRANCE TO THE ACHIEVEMENT OF FULL JUSTICE FOR THE VICTIM AND CONTINUES TO BE A THREAT TO THE DIGNITY OF FILIPINAS AND TO THE SOVEREIGNTY AS A NATION.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: D035
rows.title_short: Women's Rights
rows.abstract: UNDERSCORED THE ROLE OF FILIPINO WOMEN IN FAMILY DEVELOPMENT.  EMPHASIZED THAT THE FAMILY SHOULD BE RUN BY BOTH PARENTS IN THEIR ROLE AS FIRST TEACHERS OF THEIR CHILDREN.  CONCLUDED THAT PARENTS SHOULD VALUE THEIR CHILDREN EQUALLY REGARDLESS OF SEX AND STRESSED THE ROLE OF WOMEN IN FAMILIAL AND SOCIETAL DEVELOPMENT, WOMEN'S ACCESS TO EDUCATION AND AWARENESS OF THEIR RIGHTS, AND AN ENVIRONMENT WHICH PROMOTES GENDER EQUALITY.  POINTED OUT THAT THEY CONSIDER THEMSELVES AS AN IMPORTANT MACHINERY OF THE CONVENTION ON THE ELIMINATION OF ALL FORMS OF DISCRIMINATION AGAINST WOMEN (CEDAW).  CITED THE ANTI-TRAFFICKING OF PERSONS ACT OF 2003, ANTI-VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN AND CHILDREN ACT OF 2004 AND MAGNA CARTA OF WOMEN THAT WERE PASSED BY PAST CONGRESSES.  RENEWED COMMITMENT TO ADVANCE WOMEN'S ISSUES.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: B031
rows.title_short: Women Empowerment On Livelihood
rows.abstract: EXPRESSED CONCERN ON THE EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN WITH REGARD TO LIVELIHOOD.  TOOK PRIDE FOR THE PASSAGE OF MEASURES EMANCIPATING WOMEN AND BRIDGING INEQUITIES AND DISCRIMINATIONS BETWEEN THE TWO GENDERS.  STRESSED THAT IT IS ONLY BY MAKING WOMEN PRODUCTIVE THAT THEY CAN STAND INDEPENDENTLY AND ENJOY THE FULL BENEFITS OF THE LAW. NOTED THAT THE EXIGENCIES OF THE TIMES HAVE BRED A DILEMMA FOR THE WORKING MOTHER - WHETHER TO REMAIN AT HOME OR EARN A DECENT WAGE TO SUPPORT HER FAMILY.  EMPHASIZED THAT THE STATE SHOULD ENSURE WOMEN'S ACCESS TO LIVELIHOOD OPPORTUNITIES TO MAKE THEM PRODUCTIVE, AND TO TREAT WOMEN AS COEQUAL OF MEN.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: F058
rows.title_short: Single Parenting
rows.abstract: LAUDED WOMEN SINGLE PARENTS FOR THEIR HEROISM AS SHE CITED HOW THEY HAVE GONE THROUGH THE DAILY GRIND OF LIFE DESPITE GENDER PREJUDICE, UNEQUAL REWARD, SEXUAL HARASSMENT, JOKES AND DIRTY RUMORS, AND THE OLD CULTURAL MIND SET THAT WOMEN ARE INFERIOR.  STRESSED THAT FILIPNO WOMEN, MOST ESPECIALLY SINGLE MOTHERS, HAVE SHOWN THE SUBSTANCE AND CHARACTER THAT HAVE PRESERVED THE FILIPINO NATION
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: F096
rows.title_short: Human Trafficking
rows.abstract: STRESSED THAT THE STATISTICS ON HUMAN TRAFFICKING HAVE REMAINED GRIM DESPITE CONGRESS' PASSAGE OF THE ANTI-TRAFFICKING IN PERSONS ACT OF 2003 AND THE FORMATION OF THE INTER AGENCY COUNCIL AGAINST TRAFFICKING.  OPINED THAT ENACTING LEGISLATION WAS NOT ENOUGH TO CURB THE COMMISSION OF THE CRIME AND POINTED OUT THE NEED FOR POLITICAL WILL.  URGED HER COLLEAGUES TO ENSURE THAT THE LAWS WERE IMPLEMENTED AND THAT THE PEOPLE'S WELFARE, INTERESTS, AND DIGNITY WERE ADVANCED, SAFEGUARDED AND UPHELD AND THEIR LIVES SECURED.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: F016
rows.title_short: Babae :  Yaman Ng Bayan
rows.abstract: SPOKE ABOUT THE FAILED IMPLEMENTATION OF THE FIVE PERCENT(5%) FUNDING SCHEME FOR GENDER AND DEVELOPMENT (GAD) IN THE GENERAL APPROPRIATIONS ACT.  AFTER CITING THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THE GAD BUDGET, SHE CALLED ON THE HOUSE TO LOOK INTO THE MATTER OF NONCOMPLIANCE AND URGE DBM TO COMPEL AGENCIES TO COMPLY WITH SAID BUDGET WHICH SHE DEEMED VITAL IN ATTAINING GENDER EQUALITY AND WOMEN EMPOWERMENT, THEREBY IMPROVING THE WELFARE OF THE MARGINALIZED FILIPINO WOMEN.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: D095
rows.title_short: Women In Agriculture
rows.abstract:
SPOKE ON THE VITAL ROLE OF WOMEN FARMERS IN AGRICULTURE, CITING THEIR CONTRIBUTION IN THE CARE AND PROCESSING OF CROPS. CITED THAT THE MAGNA CARTA OF WOMEN PROVIDE WOMEN FARMERS AND RURAL WORKERS GREATER ACCESS TO CREDIT AND CAPITAL AND ALSO ENSURES THE ROLE OF WOMEN IN THE FORMULATION OF APPLICABLE FARMING TECHNOLOGIES.
STATED THAT THEY ARE CONTINUOUSLY HELPING RURAL WOMEN BY ENCOURAGING THEIR MEMBERSHIP IN FAMRERS' ORGANIZATIONS AND COOPERATIVES. CITED THAT ALMOST 90% OF THE CLIENTELE OF THE MICROFINANCE CREDIT PROGRAM OF COOPERATIVES ARE WOMEN.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: C119
rows.title_short: Association Of Feminista De Filipinas
rows.abstract: STATED THAT SHE HAS YET TO SERIOUSLY REGARD OR STUDY WHAT EFFECT HER GENDER MAY HAVE HAD ON HER CAREER.  SAID THAT THIS COULD BE DUE TO HER BELIEF THAT SHE CANNOT SIMPLY BE DEFINED BY HER WORK.  STATED THAT SHE HAS SEEN THAT WHAT TRULY MOVES WOMEN, FROM ROLE-TO-ROLE, DAY-TO-DAY EXISTENCE, IS A CORE OF CONSTANT VALUES OF FAITH, MORALITY, CHARACTER AND CAPACITY TO LOVE.  CLAIMED THAT IT IS PRECISELY THESE VALUES THAT SERVE AS THE UNIFYING RATIONALE, FOR A WOMAN'S INTEGRATION OF HER COMPLEX ROLE. SAID THAT FOR THOSE WHO HAVE BEEN BLESSED TO HAVE SERVED IN GOVERNMENT AND AS LEADERS IN BUSINESS AND SOCIETY, THEY SHOULD BE ABLE TO CELEBRATE THE MONTH OF WOMEN, WITH THEIR MEN ASSOCIATES.  AS THEY CONTINUE TO BE PART OF POLITICS, THEY SHOULD ALSO BE ABLE TO LEAVE A LASTING LEGACY WORTHY OF EMULATION. ENJOINED THE MEMBERS TO CELEBRATE WOMEN'S MONTH BY CONTINUING TO SAFEGUARD THE FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS OF EVERY PERSON IN ACCORDANCE WITH GOD'S LAWS AND THAT EACH SHOULD RESPECT HER CONDITIONS, UNDERSTAND HER PECULIARITIES AND GIVE HER THE LOVE AND CARE THAT SHE WELL DESERVES
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: F093
rows.title_short: Women's Day Against Feminization Of Labor Migration
rows.abstract: DISCUSSED THE PLIGHT OF FILIPINA OVERSEAS WORKERS AND UNDERSCORED THE NEED TO ADDRESS THE COUNTRY'S UNEMPLOYMENT PROBLEM TO AVERT THE ABUSE AND EXPLOITATION OF FILIPINOS.  RECOMMENDED THE CHANNELING OF THE BUDGET FOR DEBT SERVICING AND MILITARY EXPENDITURES TO SOCIAL SERVICES, PARTICULARLY TO HEALTH AND EDUCATION, TO ENSURE THE HOLISTIC DEVELOPMENT OF THE FILIPINO PEOPLE.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-02)

rows.author: E022
rows.title_short: Purchase Of Firetrucks Through Direct Contracting
rows.abstract: LAUDED THE EXEMPLARY EFFORTS OF THE MEN AND WOMEN OF THE BUREAU OF FIRE PROTECTION (BFP) AND OF THE MANY VOLUNTEER FIRE BRIGADES. QUESTIONED THE BUREAU'S PROCUREMENT OF 37 FIRETRUCKS AT p342 MILLION FROM 2007 TO 2008 WITHOUT BIDDING BUT THROUGH DIRECT CONTRACTING; THE DIFFERENT COSTS DESPITE HAVING THE SAME SPECIFICATIONS; THAT THE COST OF EACH WAS DOUBLED; AND THE SUPPLY OF ONE COMPANY OF ALMOST HALF OF THE PURCHASES. STRESSED THAT THE PROCUREMENT OF FIRETRUCKS DOES NOT FALL UNDER THE INSTANCES PROVIDED FOR DIRECT CONTRACTING IN THE GOV'T PROCUREMENT ACT AND ASKED FOR AN INVESTIGATION IN THE BFP CORRUPTION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2009-03-03

rows.author: E017
rows.title_short: Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program ( C A R P ) Funding
rows.abstract: TALKED ABOUT THE NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF JOINT RES. NO.19 WHICH EXTENDS THE COVERAGE OF THE AGRARIAN REFORM PROGRAM AS CONGRESS HAS FAILED TO PASS HB NO.4077 WHICH WOULD HAVE GUARANTEED FUNDING FOR LAND ACQUISITION AND DISTRIBUTION AND INCOPORATED SIGNIFICANT REFORMS.  ADDED THAT SAID JOINT RES., TOOK AWAY INSTEAD THE COMPULSORY LAND ACQUISITION AND MADE AGRARIAN REFORM OPTIONAL AND INFORMED THE BODY THAT AFTER ITS ENACTMENT, DAR ISSUED MEMORANDUM NO. 09-1804 WHICH DIRECTS TO DEFER THE PROCESSING OF COMPULSORY ACQUISITION INCLUDING THOSE LANDHOLDINGS IN THE PIPELINE AND SURVEY ACTIVITIES UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE. STRESSED THAT A HOUSE SPECIAL PANEL ON AGRARIAN REFORM SHOULD NOT BE USED AS AN EXCUSE TO FURTHER DELAY THE APPROVAL OF HB NO. 4077 AND DESECRATE THE GOALS OF THE CARP. CALLED ON THE MEMBERS TO STAND ON THE SIDE OF THE FARMERS AND APPROVE THE PASSAGE OF HB NO. 4077 AND THE REESTABLISHMENT OF THE COMPULSORY LAND ACQUISITION.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-03)

rows.author: F093
rows.title_short: Increase In Teacher's Pay
rows.abstract: TOOK THE CUDGELS FOR PUBLIC SCHOOL TEACHERS WHO WERE SEEKING A P9,000.00 RAISE IN THEIR MONTHLY SALARIES. POINTED OUT THAT THE ONLY SALRY INCREASE GRANTED THEM IN THE LAST EIGHT YEARS OF THE ARROYO ADMINISTRATION WAS INSUFFICIENT GIVEN THE NONSTOP INCREASE IN RICE AND GASOLINE PRICES.  URGED HER COLLEAGUES TO IMMEDIATELY GRANT THE TEACHERS' REQUEST AMIDST THE GLOBAL FINANCIAL CRISIS.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-04)

rows.title_short: Police Checkpoint Incident In Zamboanga Del Sur
rows.abstract: NARRATED THE EVENTS SURROUNDING WHAT HE CALLED THE INDECENT HASTE AND HIGHLY IRREGULAR IF NOT ANOMALOUS FILING OF MURDER AND ATTEMPTED MURDER CASES AGAINST 27 POLICE OFFICERS OF ZAMBOANGA DEL SUR AS A RESULT OF AN AUGUST 22, 2009 ALTERCATION IN A POLICE CHECKPOINT IN TUKURAN, ZAMBOANGA DEL SUR BETWEEN POLICE AND MILITARY ELEMENTS.  EXPLAINED THE THE CHECKPOINT WAS ESTABLISHED IN VIEW OF ATTACKS BY THE MILF IN LANAO DEL NORTE AND NORTH COTABATO. SURMISED THAT CERTAIN PERSONS, WHO HAVE NO REGARD FOR THE SAFETY OF THE PEOPLE FROM ZAMBOANGA DEL SUR, COULD HAVE PERPETRATED A FOUL PLAY.  URGED HIS COLLEAGUES TO EXAMINE THE FLAWS OF THE NATION'S CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM THAT ALLOW UNSCRUPULOUS GOVERNMENT OFFICIALS TO ABUSE THEIR FUNCTIONS.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-04)

rows.author: E032
rows.title_short: Contributions Of Dr. Aguilar
rows.abstract: SPOKE ON THE ISSUE OF BIOPIRACY AFFECTING THE COUNTRY AMIDST GLOBALIZATION WHERE RICH COUNTRIES OFTEN EMERGE AS THE USUAL WINNERS AS THEY DOMINATE GLOBAL INSTITUTIONS AND INFRASTRUCTURES AND DEVELOPING COUNTRIES END UP IN THE LOSING END. CITED TO THE BODY THE WORK OF DR. ABELARDO AGUILAR, WHO IS ONE OF THE FIRST AND THE MOST PROMINENT EXAMPLES OF BIOPIRACY. NARRATED THAT HE SENT SOIL SAMPLES TO ELI LILLY AND CO. WHICH BECAME THE SOURCE OF AN ANTIBIOTIC DRUG CALLED ERYTHROMYCIN BUT UNTIL HIS DEATH, DR. AGUILAR NEVER RECEIVED DUE RECOGNITION AND ROYALTY FROM SAID CO.. STRESSED THAT THE COUNTRY WAS ALSO DENIED THE ADEQUATE RECOGNITION AND ROYALTY ON THE DISCOVERY OF ERYHROMYCIN AS THE CONSTITUTION VESTS IN THE STATE THE ULTIMATE RESPONSIBILITY TO PRESERVE AND PROTECT THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE CONTROL AND SUPERVISION OF ITS NATURAL RESOURCES. CALLED ON HER COLLEAGUES TO SUPPORT THE FIGHT AGAINST BIOPIRACY AND ENSURE ALLOCATION OF RESOURCES TOWARDS FURTHER DEVELOPMENT OF PLANT BREEDING AND HERBAL PREPARATIONS, INTEGRATE AWARENESS ON THE SAME IN THEIR ADVOCACIES WITHIN THEIR RESPECTIVE DISTRICTS THAT WOULD RAISE THE CONSCIOUSNESS OF THE PEOPLE AND ENHANCE THE KNOWLEDGE OF INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES, AND CONDUCT PROPER INVESTIGATION ON THE IMPLEMENTATION OF EXISTING LAWS COVERING SAID ISSUE ESPECIALLY THE WILDLIFE ACT.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-03-05)

rows.author: E003
rows.title_short: Right Of Reply
rows.abstract: SPOKE ON THE ATTACK MADE BY EDITORS AND WRITERS OF THE PHIL. DAILY INQUIRER ON ITS ISSUE RELATIVE TO THE RIGHT OF REPLY BILL . CLARIFIED THAT: HE IS NOT A BLIND DEFENDER OF THE BILL; HE DOES NOT JUSTIFY THE KILLINGS OF FILIPINO JOURNALISTS AND HIS ARGUMENT IS FATALLY FLAWED READING OF REALITY. NOTED FROM THE CONTENTION OF THE EDITORIAL WRITERS THAT \"THOSE WHO KILL JOURNALISTS DO SO BECAUSE THEY HAVE SOMETHING TO HIDE\" ALSO SPEAKS OF THESE WRITERS'VIEW OF REALITY. SAID THAT NO LESS THAN THE PHIL. CENTER FOR INVESTIGATIVE JOURNALISM MADE A REPORT ON MEDIA CORRUPTION. STATED THAT HE DOES NOT AND WILL NEVER JUSTIFY, EXCUSE, NOR TOLERATE EXTRAJUDICIAL KILLING OF ANY PERSON, JOURNALIST OR NOT. CLARIFIED THAT WHAT THE BILL SEEKS IS THE RESPONSIBLE EXERCISE OF THE FREEDOM OF THE PRESS AND THE IMPORTANCE OF ONE'S FREEDOM TO EXPRESS AS IT ALSO ENCOURAGES CRITICAL YET CONSTRUCTIVE DEMOCRATIC DISCOURSE. EXPRESSED THE HOPE THAT THE EDITORIAL WRITERS WOULD DO JUSTICE TO WHAT THEIR NEWSPAPER PROFESS ABOUT \"BALANCE NEWS\".

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR WORKER'S PROTECTION, WAGE HIKE AND GOVERNMENT'S ASSISTANCE TO DISPLACED LOCAL AND OVERSEAS' WORKERS
rows.title_short: Economic Crises And Lay-offs / Wage Increase
rows.abstract: GAVE THE HIGHEST HONOR TO THE MILLIONS OF WORKERS IN AND OUT OF THE COUNTRY AND THE FARMERS IN VIEW OF THE COMMEMORATION OF THE INTERNATIONAL LABOR DAY ON MAY 1. LAMENTED THAT ONLY 10% OUT OF THE 37 MILLION WORKERS BELONG TO AN ORGANIZATION OR UNION AND ONLY 2,000 THEREOF HAS CBA AGREEMENTS WHILE 20 MILLION OFWs STRUGGLE TO WORK OUTSIDE THE COUNTRY ALL OVER THE WORLD.  STRESSED THAT THESE WORKERS ARE THE ONES WHO ARE MOST AFFECTED BY THE GLOBAL ECONOMIC CRISIS. STRESSED THAT INSTEAD OF GIVING DECEIVING PRONOUNCEMENT THAT THE CRISIS IS CONTAINED, THE GOVERNMENT MUST LOOK FOR A SOLUTION TO ITS EFFECTS ON THE COUNTRY'S LABOR FORCE WITHOUT SACRIFICING THEIR RIGHTS. CITED ILO AND NEDA STATISTICS ON UNEMPLOYMENT AS A RESULT OF THE GLOBAL FINANCIAL CRISIS AND POINTED OUT ITS REPERCUSSIONS. DECRIED LAYOFFS AS HE ALSO STRESSED THE NEED FOR A NATIONAL LEGISLATED WAGE INCREASE. CONDEMNED MALACANANG'S STATEMENT THAT THE LABOR SECTOR SHOULD NOT EXPECT ANY WAGE INCREASE. CLAIMED THAT UNSCRUPULOUS EMPLOYERS CONTINUE TO USE THE ECONOMIC CRISIS TO CONSOLIDATE THEIR PROFITS AT THE EXPENSE OF THE WORKERS.  PROPOSED A REVIEW OF ALL CASES INVOLVING WORKERS AND OFWs WHO HAVE BEEN LAID-OFF FROM THEIR JOBS AND FOR THE PREVENTION OF THE PLANNED RATIONALIZATION IN GOVERNMENT WORKERS' OFFICES.  STATED THAT FUNDS FROM THE SSS, GSIS AND OWWA SHOULD BE MADE AVAILABLE TO THE DISPLACED OFWs. UNDERSCORED THE NEED FOR CHANGES IN THE FINANCIAL AND ECONOMIC SITUATION IN THE COUNTRY AND REITERATED THE CALL FOR THE DELETION OF THE 12% vat AND THE REGULATION IN THE PRICES OF PERTROLEUM AND FOOD PRODUCTS AND BASIC UTILITIES.

rows.author: D086
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE IMMEDIATE PASSAGE OF HB 3756 (COMPENSATION TO HUMAN RIGHTS VICTIMS)
rows.title_short: On Disappearances / Human Rights Violation
rows.abstract: CALLED THE ATTENTION OF THE BODY TO THE LONG-STANDING INJUSTICE COMMITTED AGAINST POLITICAL ACTIVISTS WHO WERE ABDUCTED, TORTURED AND KILLED.  CLAIMED THAT THE OVERTHROW OF THE MARCOS REGIME WAS A STEP FORWARD IN REDRESSING THESE HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS BUT STATED THAT THE STRUGGLE FOR JUSTICE DID NOT END WITH SAID OUSTER. SAID THAT SELDA FILED A CLASS ACTION SUIT AGAINST THE MARCOSES IN THE FEDERAL DISTRICT COURT OF HAWAII FOR GROSS AND SYSTEMATTIC HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS AND SAID COURT DECIDED IN FAVOR OF THE 9,539 VICTIMS AND AWARDED THEM EXEMPLARY DAMAGES AND COMPENSATORY DAMAGES. RELATED THAT THE US SUPREME COURT UPHELD THE DECISION OF THE LOWER COURT WHICH MADE THE CLASS ACTION SUIT AGAINST FORMER PRES. MARCOS A LEGAL PRECEDENT WHICH COULD BE INVOKED BY HUMAN RIGHTS VICTIMS AGAINST HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATORS THE WORLD OVER. REITERATED THAT THESE  LED TO THE DISCOVERY AND RECOVERY OF THE SO-CALLED \"MARCOS' ILL-GOTTEN WELATH\" IN BANK ACCOUNTS IN SWITZERLAND. STATED THAT THE SWISS SUPREME COURT THEN ORDERED THE TRANSFER OF S540 MILLION TO AN ESCROW ACCOUNT AT THE PNB. ADDED THAT THE GOVERNMENT RECEIVED ANOTHER S8 MILLION FROM THE SWISS GOVERNMENT. STATED THAT CONSIDERING THAT THE SWISS SUPREME COURT ORDERED THAT THE HUMAN RIGHTS VICTIMS SHOULD BE CONSIDERED FOR COMPENSATION, THIS HAS NOT BEEN THE CASE. STATED THAT SELDA CLAIMED THAT THE ADMINISTRATION SECRETLY TRANSFERRED SAID FUNDS TO THE NATIONAL TREASURY AND IT WAS REVEALED THAT DURING THE SENATE HEARINGS ON THE \"FERTILIZER FUND SCAM\", P544 MILLION WORTH OF THE \"MARCOS ILL-GOTTEN WEALTH\" WAS RELEASED TO DAR BARELY A MONTH, BEFORE THE 2004 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTIONS.  ALLEGED THAT THE ADMINISTRATION INTENDS ON CLAIMING POSSESSION OF THE S35 MILLION DEPOSIT OF THE MARCOSES IN THE U.S. INFORMED THAT HUMAN RIGHTS VIOLATIONS VICTIMS HAVE NOT YET RECEIVED A SINGLE CENTAVO FROM THE RECOVERED \"MARCOS ILL-GOTTEN WEALTH, INSTEAD THE BENEFICIARY IS THE CURRENT ADMINISTRATION WHICH IS ITSELF A KNOWN VIOLATOR OF HUMAN RIGHTS.  STRESSED THAT THERE IS A MEASURE OF INJUSTICE FOR EVERYDAY THAT PASSES WITHOUT THE VICTIMS RECEIVING THEIR INDEMNIFICATION.  URGED THE BODY TO IMMEDIATELY CONSIDER HOUSE BILL NO.3756.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2009-04-29
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Hontiveros. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.title_short: Freedom Of Expression On Organized Labor
rows.abstract: TALKED ABOUT THE FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION OF ORGANIZED LABOR WHEREIN THE 2ND DIV. OF THE SUPREME COURT, IN THE DUSIT HOTEL CASE OF THE 29 UNION OFFICERS WHO WERE SIMPLY EXERCISING THEIR RIGHT TO SAID FREEDOM, WERE DISMISSED DESPITE THE ABSENCE OF WORK STOPPAGE. POINTED OUT THAT THE SAID COURT ALSO DISREGARDED THE LABOR CODE PROVISION THAT STRIKE IS UNDERTAKEN THROUGH WORK STOPPAGE BY WORKERS AND THE DOCTRINE THAT ALL DOUBTS SHOULD BE RESOLVED IN FAVOR OF LABOR. STATED THAT THE COURT FOUND NONETHELESS THAT THE WORKERS WERE CONSIDERED TO HAVE STOPPED WORKING SINCE THEY HAD PROVOKED MANAGEMENT INTO SUSPENDING THEM. INFORMED THE BODY THAT THE COUNTRY'S LABOR MOVEMENT IS UNITED ON SAID ISSUE AND WOULD BE FILING A COMPLAINT AGAINST THE GOVERNMENT BEFORE THE ILO FOR ITS FAILURE TO COMPLY WITH ITS STANDARDS.  URGED CONGRESS TO PASS A LAW STRENGTHENING THE RIGHTS OF WORKERS TO FREEDOM OF EXPRESSION SO THAT IT SHOULD NOT BE INTERPRETED AS WORK STOPPAGE AND TO INVESTIGATE THE NLRC ON ITS FINDINGS. ENJOINED THE MEMBERS TO SAFEGUARD THE RIGHTS OF THE WORKERS AND NOT ALLOW THE EXERCISE OF A CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHT TO BE THE BASIS OF AN ALLEGED WORK STOPPAGE.

rows.abstract: TALKED ON THE RIGHTS AND DUTIES OF THE MEMBERS OF CONGRESS IN CONNECTION WITH THE MAY 10,2010 ELECTIONS AND THE ACTIVITIES GOING ON IN THE COMELEC. DISCUSSED ABOUT THE LEGAL CONSTITUTIONAL AND LOGISTICAL IMPLICATIONS IN THE AUTOMATION OF SAID ELECTIONS SUCH AS LAWS GOVERNING THEIR CONDUCT AND WHETHER THE TOTAL AUTOMATION IS PERMISSIBLE UNDER THE PROVISIONS OF THE CONSTITUTION. EXPRESSED THAT THERE IS A REAL NEED FOR THE PASSAGE OF A SPECIAL LAW BY CONGRESS BEFORE IT CAN FULLY AUTOMATE SAID ELECTIONS, THAT THE SENTIMENT OF THE HOUSE IF FOR A PARTIAL OR MIXED AUTOMATION AND THAT THE DISBURSEMENT OF THE SUPPLEMENTAL BUDGET SHALL BE AUTHORIZED ONLY IN STRICT COMPLIANCE WITH SEVERAL PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 9369. STRESSED THAT THE COMELEC FAILED TO COMPLY WITH THE LAW, CONCLUDED THAT IT COULD NOT PROCEED WITH FULL AUTOMATION OF THE 2010 ELECTIONS WITHOUT AND ENABLING LAW.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2009-05-12

rows.author: E031
rows.title_short: Narcopolitics
rows.abstract: ROSE TO DEFEND HIS FAMILY AGAINST THE ALLEGATION OF A MANILA TIMES COLUMNIST IN AN ARTICLE THAT REP. HERMINIA B. ROMAN ALLEGED THAT GARCIAS WERE INTO NARCOPOLITICS. CLAIMED THAT IT WAS HIS FAMILY'S POLITICAL MACHINERY THAT BROUGHT REP. ROMAN TO HER SEAT IN CONGRESS AND SURMISED THAT THE LADY REPRESENTATIVE HERSELF WAS THE INFORMANT. WARNED THAT HE WILL HOLD ALL RESPONSIBLE BEFORE THE COURTS OF LAW. URGED TO CONDUCT AN EXHAUSTIVE INQUIRY INTO THE MATTER AND CLARIFIED THAT NO ONE IN HIS FAMILY IS INVOLVED IN DRUGS. STATED FOR THE RECORD THAT HE, AS WELL AS BATAAN GOV. ENRIQUE TO. GARCIA JR. AND BALANGA CITY MAYOR JOSE ENRIQUE T. GARCIA, WILL NOT BE STAYING IN THEIR RESPECTIVE OFFICES ANY MINUTE LONGER IF ANYONE CAN PRESENT EVIDENCE OF THEIR FAMILY'S INVOLVEMENT IN NARCO-POLITICS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2009-05-11
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Cerilles and Manifestation by Rep. Roman.

rows.author: F030
rows.title_short: Extortion Activities Of N P As
rows.abstract: RELATED THE TERRORISTIC ACTIVITIES OF THE NPA IN SURIGAO DEL SUR AS WELL AS IN OTHER AREAS OF THE COUNTRY AND DECRIED THEIR WIDESPREAD EXTORTION AND TERRORISTIC ACTIVITIES. RECALLED THAT HE TOO WAS A VICTIM OF THE NPA WHEN HE DID NOT ACCEDE TO THEIR DEMANDS. LAMENTED THAT THIS ILLEGAL ACTION BY THE NPA IS VERY UNFORTUNATE CONSIDERING THAT THE 2ND DIST. OF SURIGAO DEL SUR WAS RECENTLY HIT BY NATURAL CALAMITIES AND IS EXPERIENCING  UNEMPLOYMENT PROBLEMS. POINTED OUT THAT LOCAL INFRASTRUCTURES ARE BEING IMPROVED TO HASTEN AND FACILITATE THE FLOW OF GOODS AND SERVICES BUT SAID EFFORTS ARE BEING FOILED BY EXTORTION ACTIVITIES OF THE NPA. RECOMMENDED AN EXTENSIVE PROGRAM AGAINST NPA EXTORTION ACTIVITIES AND APPEALED TO THE MEMBERS TO JOIN HIM IN CONDEMNING THESE DESPICABLE ACTS.

rows.author: F105
rows.title_short: Labor Problems / Concerns
rows.abstract: DESCRIBED HOW WORKERS CELEBRATED MAY 1, LABOR DAY IN ORDER TO SHOW THEIR CONTINUING OBJECTION TO LAYOFFS IN THE MIDST OF THE GLOBAL ECONOMIC CRISIS. POINTED TO NEO-LIBERALIZATION AND CAPITALISM AS HAVING CAUSED SAID CRISIS. LIKEWISE DESCRIBED HOW THE PHILIPPINE ECONOMY FELL AS A RESULT OF THE GOVERNMENT'S CONTINUED ADHERENCE TO WORLD TRADE ORGANIZATION'S (WTO) DIRECTIVES. CRITICIZED THE ADMINISTRATION'S REACTION TO THE OIL PRICE HIKE, UNEMPLOYMENT, AND OTHER PROBLEMS SUFFERED BY ORDINARY CITIZENS: FOREIGN LOANS, TAXATION, AN ECONOMIC STIMULUS PACKAGE USING SAVINGS OF GOVERNMENT AND PRIVATE EMPLOYEES, AND AN EMERGENCY EMPLOYMENT PROGRAM GEARED TOWARDS LABOR EXPORTATION. STRESSED THAT WRONG PROGRAMS AND POLICIES AND NOT THE LABOR SECTOR'S DEMAND FOR HIGHER WAGES HAD LED TO THE LOCAL FINANCIAL CRISIS. ADVERTED FOR A REVIEW OF OIL DEREGULATION, USE OF GSIS FUNDS, AND WAGE INCREASES. NOTED THAT UNEMPLOYMENT WAS WORSENING DESPITE MALACANANG'S PRONOUNCEMENT THAT ECONOMIC FUNDAMENTALS REMAIN SOUND. OPINED THAT THE POLICY OF LABOR EXPORTATION WAS EMBARRASSING AND POINTED OUT THAT FOREIGN COMPANIES WERE BEING ALLOWED TO DOMINATE THE USE OF THE COUNTRY'S NATURAL RESOURCES.  STATED THAT THE GOVERNMENT'S CONTINUED RELIANCE ON FOREIGN INVESTMENT AND CREDIT, AND THE EXPORT OF CHEAP LABOR WOULD ONLY HASTEN THE COUNTRY'S ECONOMIC DOWNFALL AND EVEN WIDEN THE GAP BETWEEN THE RICH AND POOR. UNDERSCORED THAT WHAT THE WORKERS NEEDED FROM CONGRESS ARE MORE HUMANE AND NATIONALISTIC LAWS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2009-05-20

rows.author: F035
rows.title_short: Deactivation Of N C R Voters
rows.abstract: ASKED THE COMMITTEE ON SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS TO LOOK INTO THE PREPARATION BEING MADE BY THE COMELEC - NCR RE: THE POSSIBLE DEACTIVATION OF 1,024,745 MILLION VOTERS. CLAIMED THAT BGY. ELECTIONS ALMOST ALWAYS HAVE A LOW TURNOUT OF VOTERS COMPARED TO THAT OF THE NAT'L ELECTIONS. REITERATED HIS CALL FOR THE INVESTIGATION OF THE SAID ACTIONS OF THE COMELEC-NCR BECAUSE FAILURE TO DO SO WILL RESULT IN MASSIVE DISENFRANCHISEMENT OF VOTERS.

rows.author: C128
rows.title_short: Party List System
rows.abstract: STATED THAT THE SUPREME COURT EXPANDED THE SEATS FOR PARTY-LIST GROUPS FROM 22 TO 54 WHICH PUTS INTO EFFECT THE CONSTITUTION'S PROVISION THAT MEMBERSHIP OF CONGRESS SHALL BE ELECTED FROM LEGISLATIVE DISTRICTS AND A PARTY LIST SYSTEM OF REGISTERED NATIONAL, REGIONAL AND SECTORAL PARTIES OR ORGANIZATIONS. POINTED OUT THAT PARTY-LIST MEMBERS SHALL CONSTITUTE 20% OF THE TOTAL NUMBER OF REPRESENTATIVES AND EXPLAINED THAT THIS SYSTEM WAS CREATED TO GIVE MARGINALIZED SECTORS A VOICE IN CONGRESS. SAID THAT LOBBYING IN CONGRESS IS NOT EASY AND THAT SINCE DISTRICT REPRESENTATIVES HAVE ALREADY SO MANY THINGS TO ATTEND TO, SOMETIMES THEY FAIL TO SEE THE BIGGER CONCERNS. TALKED ABOUT THE SPIRIT OF THE PARTY LIST SYSTEM BEING UNDERMINED OR WEAKENED BY ABUSE OF SOME PERSONS OR POLITICAL GROUPS PRETENDING TO REPRESENT MARGINALIZED SECTORS WHO TAKE ADVANTAGE OF LOOPHOLES IN THE LAW TO ADVANCE THEIR POLITICAL INTERESTS AND NOT THE INTEREST OF THE UNDERPRIVILEGED. GAVE THE COMELEC GUIDELINES STATING THE QUALIFICATIONS OF A PARTY LIST GROUP AND THE DETAILS OF REGISTRATION AND POINTED OUT THE URGENT NEED TO AMEND THE ENABLING LAW REGARDING THE PARTY-LIST SYSTEM.

rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Crisologo. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F104
rows.title_short: Educational System
rows.abstract: DISCUSSED SEVERAL CONTRIBUTORY FACTORS TO THE INCREASING DROPOUT AND REPETITION RATES IN PUBLIC SCHOOLS. TALKED ABOUT THE PROBLEMS BROUGHT ABOUT BY THE EDUCATION ACT OF 1982 WHICH EMPOWERED PRIVATE SCHOOLS TO INCREASE THEIR FEES, LIKE TUITION AND MISCELLANEOUS, SO AS TO RAKE IN BIGGER PROFITS THEREBY FORCING A SUBSTANTIAL PERCENTAGE OF COLLEGE STUDENTS FROM PRIVATE SCHOOLS TO TRANSFER TO STATE UNIVERSITIES WHICH TO DATE ARE FACING SIMILAR PROBLEMS.  CONCLUDED THAT THE COMMERCIALIZATION OF THE COUNTRY'S EDUCATIONAL SYSTEM HAS RESULTED IN THE CURRENT EDUCATIONAL CRISIS.  STRESSED THAT UNLESS THE GOVERNMENT REVERSES ITS PRESENT POLICIES AND ITS THRUST TO HAND OVER TERTIARY EDUCATION TO THE PRIVATE SECTOR AND FLEXES ITS MUSCELS TO STOP UNABATED TUITION FEE INCREASES, IT WOULD BURY THE CONFIDENCE, HOPE AND FAITH OF THE FILIPINO YOUTH AND THE COUNTRY FOR A BRIGHTER FUTURE.

rows.title_short: Debt Cancellation
rows.abstract: CITED THE TRIP HE MADE TO AUSTRIA TO FOLLOW UP ON THE FREEDOM FROM DEBT COALITION'S (FDC'S) REQUEST FOR CANCELLATION OF THE PHILIPPINE DEBT ON THE AUSTRIAN MEDICAL WASTE INCINERATOR, RECAPPED THE KEY DETAILS ABOUT THE SAID LOAN. ON SAID INVESTIGATION HAS YET TO BE DRAFTED AND EMPHASIZED THAT THE PURPOSE OF THE COMMITTEE IS TO SET FORTH PRUDENT POLICIES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF AGRICULTURAL PROGRAMS AND NOT AS A FACT-FINDING BODY. rows.author: D051
rows.title_short: Hero At The Present Time, The Late Former Pres. Corazon C. Aquino
rows.abstract: Asked to declare Pres. Corazon C. Aquino a national hero through the approval of HJR No.41. Claimed that the late President rightly deserves the title as she was responsbile for restoring democracy by dismantling authoritarian rule, and for dedicating her life to the cause of the people. Stated that what distinguishes her from the rest of other comparable leaders is that even in the face of death, she continued the fight to protect and sustain the gains achieved at EDSA. Stated that as a person who campaigned against Pres. Aquino in the 1986 snap presidential elections, the highest tribute that he can bestow upon Pres. Aquino is to name her as a \"truly outstanding Filipino\". Averred that the life and death of former Pres. Aquino can have greater value and significance if every Filipino internalizes the virtues and values that she had lived for. Enjoined his colleagues to approve HJR No. 41.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2009-08-10

rows.author: F075
rows.title_short: Criteria On The Declaration Of Heroes
rows.abstract: Pointed out that no law, executive order or proclamation has ever been enacted or issued officially proclaiming any Filipino historical figure as a national hero. Noted the absence of guidelines and procedure in recognizing and declaring national heroes. Underscored that even Dr. Jose P. Rizal and the rest of the country's heroes were not explicitly declared as such. Noted that the National Historical Institute does not have the power to screen and select prospective national heroes. Asked who has the power to declare historical figures as national heroes. Urged Members to approve Joint Resolutions No. 42, 43 and 44.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2009-08-10
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Escudero and Interpellation by Rep. Lagman. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A056
rows.title_short: State Of The Nation; What Congress Should Do
rows.abstract: Stated that the President's report on the economy is completely different from what is transpiring in the country today: less productive economic sectors, increased unemployment, more appropriation for debt servicing and bigger budgetary deficits.  Claimed that the President instead, reported on the history of her Administration and presented an enticing tale of strong economy.  Cited the missing facts and omissions in the SONA.  Maintained that President's claim that her 8&1/2 years in office had been unmitigated boon to the nation deserves correction and that she failed to mention where the growth is coming from, how much government policies were responsible for it, and how it is being distributed.  Noted that the underlying support for domestic consumption has been the remittances of the OFWs remittances.  Offered some measures to quickly adopt to make the economy more resilient and productive in the long term.

rows.title_short: Pres. Gloria M. Arroyo's State Of The Nation Address ( S O N A )
rows.abstract: Referred to what he called the valedictory State of the Nation Address of the President as the most comprehensive SONA as it dealth with various subjects.  Expressed hope however that it should have tackled certain areas so as to lay the necessary policy groundwork for the succeding administration.  Specified particular national concerns and cited certain Internet articles, research studies and reports, and relevant statistical data to enlighten his colleagues as to the real situation of the country as far as the vital issues are concerned: A(H1N1); alarming demand and supply of energy; low solar energy targets; OFW and restructuring educational system to ensure a proper match between available global job opportunities and skills of Filipino graduates; and the modernization of the AFP
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2009-08-07)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Abante, Romualdo, Cojuangco.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F104
rows.title_full: NEED TO LOOK INTO THE BUSINESS PROCESS OUTSOURCING (BPO) SECTOR WHICH IS BEING USED BY COMPANIES IN DEVELOPED COUNTRIES TO EXPLOIT SKILLED BUT CHEAP LABOR IN THE COUNTRY
rows.title_short: Business Process Outsourcing ( B P O ) Sector / Call Centers
rows.abstract: Dealth with many young Filipinos being lured in entering the call center industry.  Noted that for the government, BPO sector is a major contributor in terms of revenues and employment generation.  Stressed the need to bust the myth surrounding industry and underscored that foreign companies have been exploiting the country's cheap labor that has resulted in poor quality of jobs, high turnover rate of workforce and the negative effects of the working condition to the employees.  Enjoined call centers to respect the Labor Code, and for Congress to craft laws that would protect the rights of employees.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on YOUTH AND SPORTS DEVELOPMENT since 2009-08-25

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: BIASED AND PREJUDICIAL POSTURING OF COMMISSION ON HUMAN RIGHTS CHAIR LEILA DE LIMA
rows.title_short: Statement Of The Commission On Human Rights ( C H R ) Chair
rows.abstract: Focused on the alleged bias and prejudicial posturing of CHR Chairperson Leila de Lima, her issued statements that compromised the CHR's position in formal investigations and hearings.  Noted that her pronouncements have been construed as providing protection to terrorist and criminal elemens.  Cited the alleged abduction and torture of Melissa Roxas, whom he believes is being used by the CPP-NPA-NDF in their hate campaign against the government.  Subsequently opined that Rep. Ocampo ordered the use of Ms. Roxas as the centerpiece of Bayan-USA's anti-Pres. Arroyo protest in the US.  Questioned the impartiality, neutrality and objectiveness of the CHR as mandated by the Constitution and Chairperson De Lima. Noting that those who decry human rights continually wage unabated murders of innocent Filipinos and remain scot-free. Called for among others: a congressional investigation on the CHR mandate and Chairperson De Lima, etc.; resignation of Ms. De Lima; US Gov't investigation of Bayan-USA; and the nation's fight against those who want to destroy democracy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2009-08-25

rows.author: E032
rows.title_full: RISING INCIDENCE OF HIV/AIDS IN THE COUNTRY
rows.title_short: Incidence Of H I V / A I D S Cases
rows.abstract: Talked about the worsening HIV/AIDS situation in the country.  Stated that this alarming situation is complicated by the failure of the youth to effectively protect themselves and government's failure to defend the rights of those afflicted with said disease. Made several recommendations such as: multi-sectoral approach in combating...; intensified information and education campaign...; mandate hospitals to integrate RA 8504 in their internal policies. Urged her colleagues to join in the arduous yet worthy fight against HIV/AIDS.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2009-08-25
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bello, Escudero, Zamora(R.)  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A014
rows.title_full: NEED TO ABOLISH THE PRESIDENTIAL ANTI-SMUGGLING GROUP (PASG)
rows.title_short: P A S G Activities
rows.abstract: Recalled his experience as a victim of abuse of authority by the Presidential Anti-Smuggling Group (PASG) created to help enforce customs and tariff laws. Called for the abolition of the PASG, cited several complaints and protests hurled against the Group by the very same agencies that it is tasked to assist. Pointed out that the continued existence of the PASG will hamper the effective collection of customs duties and the prosecution of smugglers and economic saboteurs.

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: APPEAL TO CONGRESS TO HELP COMFORT WOMEN ACHIEVE JUSTICE
rows.title_short: Justice For World War Two Comfort Women
rows.abstract: Plead for justice in behalf of the Filipino comfort women who were victims of sex slavery by the Japanese Imperial Army during the WW II. Underscored that she was making the manifestation on the occasion of the 64th year marking Japan's defeat by the allied forces and hoped that the said Filipinas will get the justice they deserve.

rows.author: E017
rows.title_short: Contra - S O N A
rows.abstract: Focused on the President's official trip to the United States, and criticized the lavish dinner costing one million she had with her party, emphasized that the issue is that her entourage represented a country of impoverished people. Referred to the SONA wherein the President claimed credit for the passage of the Cheaper Medicines Law as well as her promise of improving health care, providing bigger funds for education and the electrification of all barangays. Concluded that social services under Arroyo Administration does not mean delivering the basic needs of the people but dispensing patronage to allies, scholarships in exchange for votes and classrooms for kickback.

rows.title_short: Government Bidding / Procurement

rows.title_short: Gloria M. Arroyo's State Of The Nation Address ( S O N A )

rows.title_full: STRINGENT IMPOSITION OF PROGRAM GUIDELINES IN THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE LOCAL HOUSING PROGRAM OR LOCAL HOUSING FUND ALLOTMENT FOR CONGRESSIONAL DISTRICTS
rows.title_short: Local Housing Fund ( R A 7835 )
rows.abstract: Discussed the housing problem in the Philippines and the features of the Local Housing Program (LHP) as institutionalized in the Comprehensive Integrated Shelter and Finance Act (CISFA). Cited the implementation problems he encountered with the LHP when he personally availed himself of the program's benefits for his congressional district. Advanced various recommendations on how to overcome the factors impeding the smooth implementation of the program to ensure the equitable distribution of housing benefits in all the legislative districts. Exhorted the Members to attend the final hearing on the LHP guidelines for them to better understand the program and how their respective districts could avail themselves of the program's benefits.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT since 2009-08-18

rows.author: A094
rows.title_full: SHARE OF BURLEY AND TOBACCO FARMERS IN THE EXCISE TAX UNDER R.A.NO. 8240
rows.title_short: Tobacco Industry
rows.abstract: Rose on behalf of what he called a much maligned and misunderstood but important industry - the tobacco industry. Recalled that President's SONA asked Congress to approve additional excise taxes on cigarette, cigar and other tobacco products to address the burgeoning budgetary deficit of the government. Pointed out that R.A.s 8240 and 7171 are existing excise tax laws affecting the tobacco farmers wherein they have been promised a share in those tax collections so they can improve their own farming and farm-related activities. Pointed out that until now the Secretary of the DBM has yet to issue the IRR on the allocation and disbursement of these funds. Said that if Congress cannot implement existing laws, it should think twice before coming up with additional taxes and added that it should not call these taxes as \"sin\" taxes, implying that the farmers are sinful farmes because they are producing a sinful commodity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2009-08-18

rows.author: D070
rows.title_full: REPLY TO SPEECH OF REP. PALPARAN DELIVERED ON SEPTEMBER 8, 2009 RE: PEACE AND ORDER PROBLEM IN EASTERN SAMAR
rows.title_short: Previous Privilege Speech Of Hon. Palparan
rows.abstract: Denounced the allegations of Rep. Jovito S. Palparan on Sept. 8, 2009, privilege speech. Described said speech as big lie, defamatory, irresponsible, mercenary and plain braggadocio to float his Bantay Party-List in preparation for reelection in the 2010. Pointed out the incriminating lies foisted by Rep. Palparan vis-a-vis the truth about the allegations against him and his political ally, Mayor Mel Senen Sarmiento of Calbayog. Underscored that Rep. Palparan has lied and killed and has an \"axe to grind\" against him and some of the Members who voted against the impeachment of the President insinuating that they had an \"exchange deal\" with the President. Said that he is now worried for his life and of his family.

rows.remarks: Manifestation of Rep. Casino.  Referred to the appropropriate committee.

rows.author: D053
rows.title_short: Proposed Tax On Text Messages
rows.abstract: Objected to the proposal to tax text messages because this will unduly burden the poor and take away from them their source of happiness.  Claimed it is unconscionable to impose a P.50 excise tax on each and every text message and overseas call, particularly in times of adversity because the propsed tax impostion would cause an increase in the cost of text messages which would be consequently passed on to the consumers.

rows.title_full: DRUG PROBLEM AS A CONTINUING THREAT TO NATIONAL SECURITY
rows.title_short: Drug Problem

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: NEED FOR GOVERNMENT TO BE WARY OF CPP-NPA-NDF's PRONOUNCEMENTS IN VIEW OF THE RESUMPTION OF THE PEACE TALKS
rows.title_short: Peace Talk
rows.abstract: Reminded the government that its peace talks with the Maoist National Democratic Front (NDF) failed in the past because it was too complacent and ignorant about the real character and intention of a wily phantom organization.  Urged the government to: 1)ask why Mr. Jalandoni was appointed chief negotiator of the NDF panel; 2)demand a complete list of the NDF's negotiating panel; and 3) insist that the communist party comply with the provisions of the agreement on the cessation of hostilities.  Informed the Body that he would file a Resolution calling for the establisment of an international monitoring team that would supervise the implementation of any ceasefire agreement during the pendency of the peace talks.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2009-09-23
